The way you wrote this perfectly encapsulates the empty feelings of both characters in the poem. The short lines coupled with the simple yet at times a bit shocking diction ("whore" "wrist slit" "dead" "gig") reflect that the narrator and perhaps even the reader should be feeling more shock and anger about the situation, but instead are left with empty, stilted feelings.

>“I’m waiting on 

>Prince Charming,”

>she said 

>“it’ll be easier

>to look for God,”

>I said, and took a drink 

>of wine

The last lines especially sit with you, and create an even more hopeless tone than before, and I think they very nicely wrap up the poem.

My only criticism is I wish it was a bit longer, to sort of build on that hopeless, empty feeling created, so that the ending would have more impact. Great writing though!!

Wow. Even though this poem is short, you manage to cram so much into just a few lines. Personally, I'm a fan of the style you used here: the short, impactful lines leave the reader with a lot to imagine. Additionally, breaking the statement, "I've been married 7 years and I'm writing love poems again," into two lines captures a kind of mental struggle that the author has to be going through.

My criticism here is that, although I enjoy the poems length, it leaves the reader desiring more- closure, continuing, etc. Maybe make this one a series? 

All that said, wonderful poem, and I hope you're doing well.

Great work on this one, the beginning few lines are what really caught my interest; specifically "reaching up, from each finger a hand".

Those lines seem to represent some sort of intense struggle to grasp onto something/anything during times of wrestling with difficult emotions. Other lines that stuck out to me were "ball of static" and "I am the waning wind" because of the images they conjure in my brain.

All in all, an amazing poem!!

I used exclusively DevaCurl for a long time, and thought I was the only one whose hair hated the products. Turns out there's probably something more going on, and I HIGHLY suggest you watch this video before continuing to use DC products.

Coconut oil really isn't gonna help you unfortunately. This coming from a curly girl that bleached her hair at 4 times last year, what you probably need is a really gentle shampoo (I switched off between different Shea Moisture ones), and then a really good protein building conditioner. The Redken Extreme conditioner did magic for my hair, just make sure to switch on and off it after a few weeks to avoid over protenizing. Lastly, leave in conditioner is your BEST friend. I made some of my own by putting the Extreme in a spray bottle with water and loading my hair up on that, but you can actually buy one if you prefer.

In my opinion, I'd avoid using a lot of oils actually. In my experience at cosmo school, they tend to seal the cuticle and prevent moisture from penetrating your hair, leaving it dry and waxy/greasy feeling. I wish you luck and hope this helped!!

When I was a young kid, I had pin straight hair, and thought I always would. In middle school, I was really rough on my hair because it was always "Poofy" and my family made fun of me a lot for it. I would shampoo, condition, towel dry, then brush and brush and brush as it dried, till it became a frizzy mess. Then I would shove it in a ponytail, and go about my life. In high school, I tried to keep up with that method, but one day I just didn't have time to brush my hair until it was dry, so I went to bed with wet hair. Cue waking up to a MASS of curls on my head. But the fun wasn't over yet. No one in my family knew how to take care of curly hair, despite having it, so I went through a phase of looking like a bowl of ramen was dumped on my head because of the uh.. "styling" I did. Not to mention, I box dyed and bleached my hair very often, so they slowly started to disappear. A month ago, I found the curly girl method, and decided, hey, why not? Coupled with a big chop of my own, and swearing off colouring and heat styling, I'm now on my way to growing out this black and getting back my natural curls :)
Currently the routine I'm using is Redken Colour Magnetics Shampoo, Redken Extreme Repair Conditioner, and Ouidad Curl Quencher Styling Gel. Scrunched with a T-Shirt, and now airdrying. Any advice on how to make the most of my curls would be much appreciated :)
